subject: Performance intake and context-sizing — MedTechPilot integration
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Zhao <lena@medtechpilot.com>, Arjun Rao <arjun@medtechpilot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: Performance intake and context-sizing — MedTechPilot integration

Thanks again for taking the time today — good call. Quick recap of what we captured on the performance side and proposed next steps so engineering has a clean intake. Please confirm or correct any numbers below.

High-level goals (as discussed)
- p95 generation latency target: 100 ms (for short responses, streaming partials allowed)
- sustained throughput target: ~500 req/s across the cluster (peak bursts to 750/s)
- concurrency: ~200 concurrent streams/requests during daytime usage window
- streaming: required for progressive device telemetry summaries (clients want token-by-token partials)
- context window: typical input ~4k tokens, occasional long sessions up to 12k tokens (mix of input + output). Expected output sizes: 200–1500 tokens depending on the flow.

Potential performance tradeoffs we flagged on the call:
- Large context (8k–12k) increases per-token compute and KV cache pressure — will impact cold-start latencies and may push p95 beyond target without prefix caching or model shards optimized for long contexts.
- Streaming reduces tail latency for first tokens but increases concurrent kernel state (KV cache pinned longer) which affects throughput.
- Aggressive batching reduces unit cost but hurts p95; we should define acceptable batching windows (e.g., 5–10 ms) and a max tokens-per-batch cap.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Please drop a sanitized example payload for a long and short flow (we attached example_payloads.csv) — helps us quantify token distributions.
2) Confirm whether the 100 ms p95 is mandatory vs aspirational; if mandatory we will propose Dedicated capacity + prefix caching plan.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra engineer (30–45 min) — suggested times in a follow-up.

Attached: redwood_slo_template_v2.pdf (SLO fields + observability checklist)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed canary rollout and a rough cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Performance intake and context-sizing — MedTechPilot integration

Thanks Karthik — this mirrors what we captured. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The 100 ms p95 is a strict requirement only for the device-summary short flow (200–400 token outputs). For long-form clinical narrative generation (1k+ tokens), 300–400 ms p95 is acceptable.
- Streaming: clients need the first token under 80 ms if possible; otherwise partial streaming that delivers the first token quickly is fine.
- Long sessions: the 12k number reflects combined input+output; ~8–9k input is more common, and we expect the model to summarize older context aggressively (we can provide a retention rule doc).

We’ll upload two sample payloads to the Drive link you shared (one short, one long). Our infra lead Arjun will also join the deep-dive.

—Lena

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: initial perf notes for MedTechPilot (do not forward external)

Brief internal take:
- If device-summary must hit 80–100 ms p95 with streaming first-token <80 ms, Hosted single-tenant won’t be enough at scale; recommend Dedicated with pinned KV-cache nodes + low-latency network fabric.
- For typical input distributions (median ~4k, 95th ~9k), we should enable prefix/KV caching and a sliding-window summarize policy to prune old context server-side. That will limit effective sequence lengths for the heavy tail.
- Quantization: 4-bit (q4) for middle-tier reduces memory but watch for quality delta on clinical text. We can propose two model variants (fp16 for long/high-quality flows, q4 for short/interactive flows) and route by traffic class.
- Batching policy: soft batching window = 8 ms, max tokens-per-batch = 2048. Add a latency-first preemptive path for streaming-first-token routes.

I’ll draft an ops runbook for canarying and cost projections after we get the sample payloads.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Morning — thanks, Lena. Proposed next steps and scheduling:
- Technical deep-dive (45 min) — options: Tue 2026-11-17 09:00–09:45 PT or Wed 2026-11-18 13:00–13:45 PT. Please confirm preferred slot.
- Action: MedTechPilot to upload two representative payloads (short/long) to the Drive link; we’ll baseline token counts and simulate p95 under multiple configs.
- I attached the SLO template (redwood_slo_template_v2.pdf) and a short intake checklist. We’ll ask Arjun to confirm on-network constraints (NAT, egress rules) so we can size Dedicated placement.

Operational asks for the deep-dive:
1) One sample long trace with timestamps and expected output size (we need to model KV cache hit rates).
2) Expected daily request distribution (hourly shape) and retention window for context.
3) Any regulatory constraints on model choice or quantization — PHI handling notes if applicable.

If the 80 ms first-token target is a hard SLO for the short flow, we should flag this as an escalation and propose a warmed Dedicated pool in the same cloud region. We’ll include rough cost deltas in the follow-up email.

Thanks — I’ll send a calendar invite once Lena confirms.

—Marissa

Appreciate the clear notes. Two quick datapoints from infra: 
- Typical short flow payload (post-tokenize) ~350 tokens input, ~300 tokens output. Long flow can be as high as 9k input + 1k output in rare cases; median long is ~6k input.
- Our current app-level timeout is 2s; we can raise it to 5s for long-form endpoints during rollout.
- Network: VPC peering is possible (we can do Private), but we’ll need to review egress policies.

We uploaded example_payloads.csv to the Drive link and left a sample long trace. Happy to join Tue 11/17 at 09:00 PT.
